title: Smoothness of Bring's surface and resolution of spacetime defects
html:
Remark. Smoothness of Bring's surface and resolution of spacetime defects

Bring's surface \mathcal{S} (Bring's surface) is a smooth algebraic variety. The three power-sum constraints intersect transversely in \mathbb{P}^4, ensuring no singular points exist. The six topological defects identified in color bundles—where the discriminant \Delta(z) vanishes and two color sheets X_i,X_j collide—are singularities of the projection \pi\colon\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}), not of the surface itself.

Resolution in the x_j coordinates. At a branch point z=z_c where x_2=x_3, define the local color coordinate \delta=x_2-x_3. In a neighbourhood of the defect, the spacetime ratio satisfies

  z-z_c \sim \delta^2.

While the projection map develops a ramification cusp, \delta passes smoothly through zero, carrying the geometry from one sheet to the other. The exceptional divisor of the blow-up at each branch point sits already embedded in the color coordinates x_2,x_3,x_4. No external resolution is required.

Resolution in the w_k coordinates. The DFT mixes all five x_j into every resolvent w_k (Lagrange resolvents). Thus no single w_k vanishes at a branch point. The Briggs--Klein chart (Briggs--Klein chart) remains smooth throughout 0<r<\infty. The radial parameter r=\lvert w_1\rvert^2 is regular on \mathcal{S}, and the C_5 orbits w_k\mapsto\zeta^k w_k foliate the surface without fixed points. The infinite torsion and eigenvalue crossings visible in the base \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) are artefacts of projecting away the internal degrees of freedom that the w_k retain.
